name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Stand about two steps in front of a bench, holding a dumbbell in each hand, and rest the top of your back foot on the bench.
Keep your torso tall and lower straight down until your back knee nearly touches the floor and your front thigh is about parallel to it.
Push through the whole front foot to stand back up, keeping the front knee in line with your toes.
Do all reps on one leg, then switch. Leaning slightly forward puts more work on the glutes.

name: Pendulum Squat
instructions: Step onto the platform with your back against the pad and your shoulders under the shoulder pads, feet about hip-width apart.
Release the safety and bend your knees, letting the sled swing down and back until your knees are deeply bent.
Drive through your feet to push the sled back up without locking your knees hard at the top.
Re-engage the safety when you're done.

name: Belt Squat
instructions: Attach the belt around your hips and stand on the platform with your feet slightly wider than hip-width.
Hold the handles for balance, keep your chest up and squat down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Stand back up by pushing the floor away. The load hangs from your hips, so your spine stays unloaded.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs, feet hip-width apart and knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and let the dumbbells slide down the front of your legs, keeping your back flat.
Go down until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, usually around mid-shin.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.

name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Hinge at the hip, letting the free leg travel straight back as the dumbbell lowers toward the floor. Keep your hips square.
Lower until your torso is close to parallel with the floor or you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Return to standing by driving the hip forward, then finish the reps before switching legs.

name: Machine Hip Thrust
instructions: Sit in the machine with your upper back against the pad and the hip pad or belt across your hips, feet flat and shoulder-width apart.
Tuck your chin and drive your hips up until your thighs and torso form a straight line.
Squeeze your glutes hard for a moment at the top, then lower under control.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
instructions: Set a bench next to the smith machine, sit on the floor with your upper back against it and the padded bar over your hips.
Plant your feet shoulder-width apart so your shins are vertical at the top.
Unrack and drive your hips up until your body is straight from shoulders to knees, squeezing your glutes.
Lower until your hips are just above the floor and repeat.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Set the bar at mid-thigh height and stand close to it, gripping it just outside your legs.
Unrack, soften your knees and push your hips back, lowering the bar along your thighs with a flat back.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, then drive your hips forward to stand tall.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under a bench, a loaded bar or a partner's hands.
Keep your body straight from knees to head and slowly lean forward, resisting with your hamstrings for as long as you can.
Catch yourself with your hands when you can no longer hold the position, then push off lightly and pull yourself back up with your hamstrings.
Make it easier by holding a band from above, or by only doing the slow lowering.

name: Reverse Nordic
instructions: Kneel upright on a pad with your knees hip-width apart and the tops of your feet on the floor.
Keeping a straight line from your knees to your head, lean back slowly as far as you can control.
Use your quads to bring yourself back up to upright. Don't bend at the hips.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and loop it around the ankle farther from the machine.
Stand side-on to the machine holding it for balance, with your working leg slightly in front of the other.
Lift the leg out to the side without leaning your torso, then lower slowly back across.

name: Tibialis Raise
instructions: Lean your back against a wall with your heels about a foot in front of you and your legs straight.
Pull your toes and the balls of your feet up toward your shins as high as you can.
Lower them slowly without letting them slap the floor. Step farther from the wall to make it harder.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width, a kettlebell on the floor about a foot in front of you.
Hinge, grab the handle with both hands and hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it up to chest height; your arms only guide it.
Let it fall back between your legs, hinging to absorb it, and go straight into the next rep.

name: Assisted Pull-Up Machine
instructions: Set the counterweight: the more weight you select, the more help you get.
Kneel or stand on the platform and take a shoulder-width overhand grip on the handles.
Pull your chest up toward the handles, driving your elbows down to your sides.
Lower all the way until your arms are straight. Reduce the assistance as you get stronger.

name: Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand over a barbell on the floor, feet hip-width apart, and hinge until your torso is about parallel to the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with a flat back.
Row the bar explosively to your lower chest without raising your torso.
Lower it back to a dead stop on the floor before each rep.

name: Seal Row
instructions: Lie face down on a raised flat bench with the barbell (or two dumbbells) on the floor below you.
Grip the bar a little wider than shoulder-width and let your arms hang straight.
Pull the bar up to the underside of the bench, squeezing your shoulder blades together, while your chest stays on the pad.
Lower under control to a full stretch.

name: Meadows Row
instructions: Wedge one end of a barbell in a corner or landmine and load the other end.
Stand side-on to the end of the bar in a staggered stance and grab the sleeve overhand with the hand farther from it.
Brace your free forearm on your front knee and row the bar up and back toward your hip.
Lower to a full stretch, finish the reps, then switch sides.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
instructions: Adjust the seat so the chest pad sits at mid-chest and you can just reach the handles with straight arms.
Keep your chest on the pad and pull the handles toward you, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together for a moment, then let the handles go forward to a full stretch.

name: Single-Arm Cable Row
instructions: Attach a single handle to a mid or low pulley and sit or stand facing it.
With one arm extended and your torso upright, row the handle to your side, keeping the elbow close.
Let your shoulder reach forward on the way back for a full stretch, finish the reps, then switch arms.

name: Single-Arm Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set a handle on a low pulley and stand side-on to the machine, holding the handle with the hand farther from it.
With a slight bend in the elbow, raise your arm out to the side until it's about level with your shoulder.
Lower slowly until the hand is in front of your hips, finish the reps, then switch sides.

name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Adjust the seat so your shoulders line up with the machine's pivot points and the pads rest on the outside of your upper arms.
Raise your arms out to the sides until they're level with your shoulders.
Lower under control without letting the weight stack touch down between reps.

name: Landmine Press
instructions: Wedge one end of a barbell in a landmine or corner and load the other end.
Stand facing the bar in a split or square stance and hold the end of the bar at your shoulder with one or both hands.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight, then lower it back to your shoulder.
The angled path is easier on the shoulders than a strict overhead press.

name: Cable Y-Raise
instructions: Set two low pulleys without handles, cross the cables and hold the ends, or use one cable for one arm at a time.
Stand between the pulleys and raise your arms up and out into a Y shape above your head, thumbs up.
Lower slowly back to the start. Keep the weight light and the movement controlled.

name: Bayesian Cable Curl
instructions: Attach a handle to a low pulley, face away from the machine and hold the handle with your arm behind your body.
Step forward into a staggered stance until there's tension on the cable with your arm stretched back.
Curl the handle forward and up without moving your elbow forward, then lower to a full stretch behind you.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

name: Cable Triceps Kickback
instructions: Attach a handle or the bare cable to a low pulley and hinge forward facing the machine.
Hold the cable with your upper arm pinned to your side and your elbow bent.
Straighten your arm back behind you, squeeze the triceps, then let the forearm swing back down under control.
Finish the reps, then switch arms.

name: Dead Hang
instructions: Grab a pull-up bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms and relaxed shoulders.
Hold for time, keeping your breathing steady. Log the seconds held as reps.

name: Copenhagen Plank
instructions: Lie on your side next to a bench and place your top leg on it, the bench under your inner knee or ankle.
Prop yourself up on your forearm and lift your hips until your body is straight; the bottom leg hangs free or lifts toward the bench.
Hold, then switch sides. Supporting at the knee is easier than at the ankle.

name: Cable Woodchopper
instructions: Set a handle on a high pulley and stand side-on to the machine, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the handle with both hands above your near shoulder and arms almost straight.
Rotate your torso and pull the handle diagonally down across your body to the outside of the far knee, pivoting on your back foot.
Return under control, finish the reps, then switch sides.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms.
Without swinging, pull your knees up toward your chest, curling your pelvis up at the top.
Lower your legs slowly until they're straight again.
